newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close up on technical rebound.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close up on technical rebound.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed up on Monday on a technical rebound after a sharp falls last Friday due to Beijing's announcement of a ban on state banks trading stocks, traders said.
The index gained 0.811 points or 0.95 percent to 86.148 on thin volume of 8.7 million shares worth $6.1 million.

The index lost 4.34 percent last Friday after the People's Bank of China, the central bank, ordered state banks to offset their existing stock positions within 10 days and stop trading on the state debt repurchase and spot market immediately.
"The day's rise was mainly due to a technical rebound," said a trader. "Market sentiment was cautious after Friday's falls, making trading volume very thin."
"After sharp falls last Friday, a little bargain-hunting set in on Monday, pushing up the index," said a second trader. "The short-term market trend will depend on new market-moving news."
Of 43 B shares, 36 traded on Monday, with 20 up, five flat and 11 down.
Bicycle maker Shanghai Phoenix Co was the star performer on a technical rebound, jumping $0.012 or 9.37 percent to $0.140 on volume of 100,000 shares.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi Co was the second biggest gainer on institutional support buying, closing up $0.080 or 8.88 percent to $0.980 on volume of 345,700 shares.

Market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co was the most actively traded, falling $0.004 or 0.27 percent to $1.432 on volume of 1.4 million shares due to profit-taking by domestic investors.

Shanghai's A share index ended slightly down on cautious sentiment after the recent official crackdown on the stock markets and amid market talk that further measures would be introduced to cool down trading, traders said.
The index lost 0.769 points or 0.06 percent to 1,331.168 on volume of 327.3 million shares worth 4.7 billion yuan.
The SSE 30 blue-chip index dipped 28.341 points or 0.71 percent to 3,957.031 points.
Newcomer Wuhan Dangdai Hi-tech Co was the worst performer on profit-taking, plunging 1.83 yuan to end at the 10-percent limit-down level of 16.47 yuan on volume of 599,500 shares.
